subject: AWS Marketplace listing copy + layout questions / procurement note
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Miller <sophie.miller@aws-partner.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: AWS Marketplace listing copy + layout questions / procurement note

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the intro to CloudOps. I’m attaching our current product page draft and a tile layout mock (tile-layout-v3.png). We’re getting close but have a couple of blocking items before we schedule the final validation with the marketplace team: 

1) Copy density: the marketplace UX trims long feature lists; we need a shortened 140–180 char description that still calls out latency/cost differentiation. Laura, can you propose two variants (concise + friendly) by EOD Monday?
2) Pricing footnotes: CloudOps procurement wants an explicit footnote about reserved capacity vs on-demand billing and a sample invoice line. Aditya, can you draft a one-line footnote we can include?
3) Tile imagery & SKU mapping: AWS asked for a single hero tile for the AMI + listing tile with clear usage examples. Kimberly, can you confirm whether the current tile has the correct dimension and whether the trial CTA maps to the PrivateOffer SKU we discussed?

We’d like to get these resolved so Sophie can run the preflight with the AWS onboarding team next week.

Thanks —
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Marketplace GTM | Redwood Inference
nikhil_sharma@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment stubs: redwood-aws-productpage-draft.docx (docx), tile-layout-v3.png (image), pricing-footnotes.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Date: Fri, 06 Jan 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace listing copy + layout questions / procurement note

Hi Nikhil —

Got the attachments, thanks. Quick notes from the AWS preflight checklist: 
- Short description: keep to ~160 chars and avoid comparative claims like "cheaper than X"; you can mention "cost-optimized inference with latency SLOs".
- Hero tile: recommended dimension 1200x600 PNG; thumbnails will be cropped to 16:9 so keep the CTA and logo centered. Tile-layout-v3 looks promising but move the small text out of the lower 10% of the canvas.
- SKU mapping: marketplace requires a clear mapping doc that ties each SKU to an entitlement (Trial / PrivateOffer / BYO). Can you produce a simple table?
- Procurement asks: AWS prefers a single-line footnote for the listing plus a downloadable sample invoice for procurement review.

I’ll block 30 mins on Jan 12 for the AWS onboarding review if you can have the revised assets in by EOD Jan 11. Danielle from CloudOps is copied to confirm procurement cadence.

Cheers,
Sophie
Sophie Miller | Partner Development Manager, AWS
sophie.miller@aws-partner.com

Nikhil / team —

Attached are two short-description variants and a 2-sentence elevator blurb you can drop into the listing. I kept the language compliant with marketplace policy (no named comparisons).

Variant A (Concise, technical): "Cost-optimized LLM inference runtime with predictable latency SLOs, KV-caching, and autoscaling for production apps."
Variant B (Friendly, product): "Run high-throughput LLM inference with predictable latency and lower unit cost—tuned for production web and API workloads."

Elevator (2-sentence): "Redwood Inference delivers a high-throughput, production-grade inference runtime that balances latency and cost via smart batching and KV caching. Deploy hosted, dedicated, or private modes with consistent APIs and rollout controls."

Notes: Kept the char counts under 180 for both variants. I also removed the phrase "SLA-backed" from the short blurb since that’s an enterprise contract term; we can mention SLA in the dedicated product page copy instead.

I pasted the short descriptions at the bottom of redwood-aws-productpage-draft.docx and updated the hero CTA copy to "Start free trial" (maps better to AWS trial flow).

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Writer | Redwood Inference

Team —

Draft footnote for the listing and a suggested invoice line below. Danielle / CloudOps procurement: please confirm if this aligns with your requirements or if you need alternate wording.

Listing footnote (single-line): "Billing options include on-demand usage and reserved capacity subscriptions; reserved capacity commitments are billed per the PrivateOffer contract."

Sample invoice line (example):
Redwood Inference — PrivateOffer: Reserved GPU capacity (monthly) — Qty 1 — $12,000 — Subscription period: Jan 2028

If CloudOps needs us to add specific tax or legal phrasing we can iterate, but this should satisfy the marketplace sample requirement.

We can join the AWS onboarding call on Jan 12 at the time Sophie proposed; Danielle (me) and one procurement engineer will attend.
